order.why_here: The simplest converging walk: compare mirror cells from both ends, skipping junk.
Introduces the reader/writer geometry: a writer trails the reader and swaps kept values forward.
Converging pointers that produce output: the largest |x| is always at an end, so fill from the back.
Slow/fast with a look-back: the writer checks its own output two cells back instead of counting.
Three pointers: one reader and two writers growing from opposite ends keep four regions.
Makes the pruning argument explicit: each comparison deletes a whole row or column of pairs.
Sort, fix an anchor, run Two Sum II on the suffix; sorted order also makes dedup local.
No sorting: the monotone fact is geometric, the shorter wall can never be in a better pair.
The shorter-side argument plus running maxima settles one cell of water per step.
Pointers on two strings plus one bookmark: the latest star dominates every earlier one.
